title: Anyone here using Codeium? I ran out of my trial in Cursor and ran out of GitHub Copilot for the month... What alternatives do I have?
author: Hot_Cause8918
selftext:
So Claude is super expensive, and im not going to use that...

I thought Cursor would renew like Github Copilot, unfortunately it doesnt seem that way...

So any suggestions? Should I go for Codeium? I heard its not as good as Copilot / Cursor / Claude.

Its really sad that Claude is so expensive.

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: Just shill out $20 for cursor, it’s worth it and to be able to set it to use composer 2 is game changing. Was able to get a 3D forest with a village in it as a scene and create a door that transitions to the next scene and walking mechanics and the ability to hold a torch. It’s pretty good

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body: 20$ a month, right? Okay will try that. But did you try Codeium? Its free... If it does almost the same thing, I dont mind to code by myself any small flaws it has left to fix.

replies.author: tomByrer
replies.body: Cursor & Codeium are both VSCode forks.  Codeium if you want more privacy (I plan to use that for local AI), Cursor if you want better AI capabilities.

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body: Cursor is great. Though i can barely tell the difference between Cursor and Github Copilot they are similar. But Cursor trial expired in like 3 days. So now im looking for an alternative. I installed Ollama + Qwen, with Continue.dev and so far its a bit clunky. Its quite demanding in terms of resources, and it was a pain to install it. I kind of want to uninstall it.

replies.author: tomByrer
replies.body:
Running local AI is demanding.  I have a seperate GPU (RTX3090) & harddrive that is only for running AI.  I've only tried small model Qwen, but seems not smart if you want something weird.  I need to try bigger version of Qwen.

Also you can buy tokens via APIs.  
I think the best plan is a mixture of 2, but I haven't gotten that far yet.

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body: I think i will stick with Qwen and Windsurf, then use Copilot and Cursor when its free. I will make up for anything missing with my own skills hopefully. Thanks.

replies.author: TheRealRedditHermit
replies.body: What engine are you using out of curiosity?

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Unity, I tried all those ai game studio stuff like revoltgpt.dev and google ai studio, I prefer loading cursor up into unity if I’m going to pay $20 for an ai to generate what I want. Those studio app AIs only give you so much you can do.

comments.author: ShapeSim
comments.body: I use WIndsurf. It's good. Of course not gonna lie when it gets stuck it gets stuck, but hey you are supposed to do some handholding

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body: Did you try Github Copilot or Cursor. Is it similar? Or its worse? thanks

replies.author: ShapeSim
replies.body: only the free ones. Perhaps very slightly, or better at one prob but worse at others.

comments.author: JohnySilkBoots
comments.body: Claude is expensive because it’s good. The amount of time I save using it is truly worth the money.

comments.author: mikecrash
comments.body: Is cursor better than the  CC extension in vs code?

comments.author: BillBangkok
comments.body: Codex also a great choice, more token to spent, higher usage than claude and current 5.4 codex high is working well (model before this for me it not worth to working with at all). Cons is it slower than claude and even on fast feel slow, I'm on 20$ plan and still didnt hit weekly limit yet.

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body: Its not free, right? Does it have monthly free stuff like github copilot? How does it compare to Cursor?

replies.author: BillBangkok
replies.body:
It’s not free. If you’re looking for free options, I think only Cursor and Windsurf show promising results. Compared to Cursor, if you’re still at the stage of choosing a model, Cursor might be the better option because it offers a wide variety of models to choose from. However, you may hit token limits faster, since some models consume more tokens.

You could start by trying Cursor (free) for prototyping—it works well at that stage. But if you’re ready to invest around $20, I would rank them as: Codex > Cursor > Claude.

On the other hand, if you have a larger budget (around $200), I’d recommend: Claude > Cursor > Codex. So far, Claude has been the best for coding in my experience.

That said, the best choice really depends on how you work, your preferences, workflow, and use case all play a big role.

replies.author: Hot_Cause8918
replies.body:
Cursor > Claude? Its the first time i hear this. Everyone says that Claude is way better than Cursor. Ahh it seems you are evaluating it based on other parameters than just performance. Like tokens and things like that, right?

\> So far, Claude has been the best for coding in my experience.

Exactly.

Thanks. And what do you think about this system:

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7AImkA96mE8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7AImkA96mE8)

Basically, its Continue .dev with Ollama and Deepseek R1 and Qwen 2.5b. So far seems to be working well.

replies.author: BillBangkok
replies.body: Claude was great, but with the $20 plan you can hit the weekly limit in just one or two days, even when using it for hobby work, so I don’t think it’s good value for money. As for open-source models, my Mac (I’m still using an Intel-era machine) can’t process more than 4 tokens per second, so I can’t really use them. I might give them a try if I had a more powerful Mac or PC.
